# staark

A small reactive DOM renderer. Use Staark when an application should own a mutable state object, automatically rerender after state mutations, and reconcile an abstract node tree with the DOM.

## Runtime and builds

Staark runs in browsers and requires DOM APIs. The package entry exports `mount`, `node`, `memo`, `conditional`, `match`, `nde`, `factory`, `fctory`, and `identifier`.

The base browser build contains `mount`, `node`, and `memo`. The full browser build adds the helper functions. Package imports are tree-shakeable, so unused helpers can be removed by a bundler.

Names such as `n`, `c`, and `m` are conventional local import aliases, not package exports:

```JavaScript
import {
  conditional as c,
  match as m,
  node as n,
} from '@doars/staark'
```

## Types

```TypeScript
type NodeContent = string | MemoAbstract | NodeAbstract

type ResolveFunction = (
) => NodeContent[] | NodeContent | null | undefined
```

## `mount`

```TypeScript
mount(
  rootElement: HTMLElement | Element | string,
  renderView: (state: Record<string, any>) => NodeContent[] | NodeContent,
  initialState?: Record<string, any> | string,
  oldAbstractTree?: NodeContent[] | string | null,
): [
  update: () => Promise<void>,
  unmount: () => void,
  state: Record<string, any>,
]
```

Mounts a view on an element. A string root is treated as a query selector. If it does not match, Staark appends a new `div` to `document.body` and uses that element.

The initial state defaults to `{}`. A plain object is wrapped in a recursive proxy; mutations schedule a microtask render. A supplied proxy is used directly, so call `update()` when its mutations should render. State proxies created by `mount` are always recognised; other proxies are detected with `structuredClone`; a proxy whose contents can not be cloned (for example functions) is not detected and is wrapped instead. Serialized initial state is parsed as JSON.

`oldAbstractTree` hydrates existing DOM produced by `@doars/staark-isomorphic`. A serialized tree is parsed as JSON. When no old tree is supplied, the root's existing children are converted into an abstract tree before reconciliation.

`update()` schedules a render and returns its promise. `unmount()` removes all rendered children and disables further updates. The returned state is the same proxy passed to the view and event listeners.

## `node`

```TypeScript
node(
  type: string,
  attributesOrContents?: NodeAttributes | NodeContent[] | NodeContent,
  contents?: NodeContent[] | NodeContent,
): NodeAbstract
```

Creates an abstract DOM node. The second argument is treated as contents when it is a string, array, or abstract node, so both forms are valid:

```JavaScript
node('p', 'Text')
node('button', { click: onClick }, 'Save')
```

Attribute behavior in the DOM renderer:

- Function values are event listeners. They receive `(event, state)`. Define stable listener functions outside the view when practical so they can be reused between renders.
- `class` accepts a string, an array joined with spaces, or an object whose truthy keys become class names.
- `style` accepts a CSS string or an object. Camel-case properties are assigned through `element.style`; names containing hyphens use `style.setProperty`.
- `value` updates both the attribute and live element property.
- `null`, `undefined`, and `false` remove or omit an attribute.
- Attributes, classes, and styles are compared with the previous render rather than read back from the DOM, so only changed values are written. Changes made to them outside staark are kept until the rendered value changes. Only own properties of attribute and style objects are applied.
- `key` is sibling reconciliation metadata and is never written to the DOM. Keys must be stable and unique among siblings.

## `memo`

```TypeScript
memo(
  render: (state: Record<string, any>, memory: any) => NodeContent[] | NodeContent,
  memory: any,
): MemoAbstract
```

Reuses a rendered subtree while the render function identity is stable and `memory` remains equal. A copy of `memory` is kept, so state objects mutated in place are compared with their previous contents. Arrays and plain objects are compared by content and dates by time; maps, sets, class instances, and other objects only by identity, as are circular references. Memos sharing a render function, such as those rendering the items of a list, are matched by their `memory` first and their order second, so mapping state items to memos reuses unchanged items even after reordering. Define the render function outside its parent view. Nested memo nodes are discouraged because memo caches are cleared after updates. Unchanged memo contents are not diffed again, so changes made to their DOM outside staark are kept.

## View helpers

```TypeScript
conditional(
  condition: any,
  onTruth: NodeContent[] | NodeContent | ResolveFunction,
  onFalse?: NodeContent[] | NodeContent | ResolveFunction,
): NodeContent[]

match(
  key: any,
  lookup: Record<any, NodeContent[] | NodeContent | ResolveFunction>,
  fallback?: NodeContent[] | NodeContent | ResolveFunction | null,
): NodeContent[]
```

`conditional` selects one branch. `match` selects a lookup value or fallback. A selected function is evaluated lazily. Both functions normalize the selected content to an array.

## Alternative node creation

```TypeScript
nde(selector: string, contents?: NodeContent[] | NodeContent): NodeAbstract
```

`nde` parses compact selector syntax such as `a.button#next[href=/next]`. `factory` provides tag-name functions around `node`; `fctory` provides tag-name functions combined with selector parsing.

```JavaScript
import { factory, fctory, nde } from '@doars/staark'

const { div } = factory
const { a } = fctory

div([nde('strong.notice', 'Notice')])
a('.button[href=/next]', 'Next')
```

## Example

```JavaScript
import { mount, node } from '@doars/staark'

const increment = (event, state) => {
  state.count++
}

const [update, unmount, state] = mount(
  '#app',
  (currentState) => node('button', { click: increment }, currentState.count),
  { count: 0 },
)
```

For server rendering, use `@doars/staark-isomorphic` and pass its serialized state and tree to `mount`. When state and scheduling are managed elsewhere, use `@doars/staark-patch` instead.
